thread:
samir: Quick heads-up — I'm opening a tiny PR to add a migration note for pipeline prefetch compatibility with some quant profiles. Not urgent but want a quick sweep from docs + ML infra before merge.

maria: Can you sketch the user-visible problem so I can write the blurb?

samir: TL;DR: streaming pipelines that enabled aggressive prefetch + 4-bit quant profiles can cause out-of-order KV cache priming and occasional latency spikes for short-prefix workloads. Users see 50-200ms tail spikes on first token.

jun: Is this the issue where prefetch pulls full KV pages before model warms up? We saw that in the perf tests.

samir: Exactly. The prefetch heuristic assumed linear KV growth; with grouped attention in q4_fast it overshot and triggered async GC in the runtime.

sasha: I can add a small e2e snippet in the examples folder showing the safe config. Want me to also add a unit test harness?

samir: Yes please. Test harness would be great. The minimal docs change: short note in the migration guide + an SDK snippet showing `prefetch: false` for those profiles + a recommended fallback `prefetch: heuristic`.

maria: Suggest a 3-line checklist for the PR: 1) short problem paragraph, 2) code snippet, 3) link to test results and CI. Also add a small NOTE callout about latency vs throughput tradeoff.

samir: Agreed. Here's the snippet I plan to include (copyable):

```
# migration example: safe prefetch toggle for q4_fast
optimize.pipeline.update(
  model="redwood/q4-fast-v2",
  prefetch={"enabled": false},
  rollout="canary"
)
```

jun: For the SDK example, we should show both JS and Python. e.g. Python: `client.optimize.update(..., prefetch={"enabled": False})`. I can paste the JS later.

maria: Where should the PR live? docs repo path and a short label?

samir: Path: `docs/optimize/migration/` — file `prefetch-quant-compat.md`. Label: `docs:optimize-migration` + `needs-ml-review`. Add `qa` for a quick smoke.

sasha: I'll implement the e2e harness in `examples/optimize/prefetch-smoke` and include a small script that runs with `--profile q4_fast`.

samir: Sweet. One more thing — include a tiny perf graph link so reviewers can verify numbers: https://internal.redwood/perf/1872-prefetch-q4fast (public link later).

maria: I'll draft the blurb and push a PR branch `docs/prefetch-compat-1824001234`. Will @mention you all in the PR.

jun: When you push, please add the flaky-tolerant label; this touches timing-sensitive examples.

docs-bot: PR created: https://git.redwood/repo/docs/pull/3124 by maria — labels: docs:optimize-migration, needs-ml-review.

samir: Nice — I'll review after lunch. @sasha can you link the test output as an artifact in the PR? :eyes: :rocket:

sasha: Yep will upload `prefetch-smoke.tar.gz` to the PR artifacts.

maria: Thanks everyone — aiming to merge after one ML + one Docs sign-off.

samir: If any of you spot wording that overpromises, flag it. Keep it actionable and reversible.

jun: Quick note for the changelog: call out "prefetch behaviour change for q4 profiles" under Optimize v2 migration.

maria: Got it. I'll add a changelog bullet.

samir: Closing the loop here — will post merge + cherry-pick instructions to #eng-ml once merged. Thanks all.
